transcript: I was really nervous to go back to John Proctor as the villain, because, as I've mentioned many times on here, this was my favourite show of last season. It's my favourite play on Broadway. But it can be a really scary thing when you have such a finely tuned ensemble like this one and you have someone leave, in this case, Sadie Sink, and a new member come in, in this case, Chiara Aurelia. Now, I know some people know Kiara from Fear Street or Cruel Summer, but I haven't seen either of those, so she was a completely unknown factor to me. But I am happy to report I thought she was fantastic, and the play is just as good as ever. Her Shelby is very different from Sadie. So I will admit, at first I was a little bit thrown off. But once I was able to get Sadie's voice out of my head and buy into Kiara's Shelby for what it was rather than what it wasn't, I was fully bought in. Shelby is a little bit more desperate, a little bit more dramatic, a little bit more tomboyish, and it does change the dynamic that she has with some of the other girls, particularly her dynamic with Raylan, which is in many ways the heart of the show. Like the finale of this play fully hinges on that dynamic. But even though that dynamic feels a little bit different, the end of this play still Hits just as hard as it ever has. And that is in part yes to Kimberly Bellflower's incredible script and the amount of depth that she has imbued these characters with. But also Kiara for being able to join this well oiled machine and bring her own spin to it. As well as the rest of the actors for being able to adjust their performances in subtle ways to fit this new ingredient. And so I am very happy to say that this show still comes highly recommended by me. If you saw it with Sadie, now is a really good time to go back. And if you were debating not going because Sadie is no longer in it, I still think it's well worth your time.
